The Client as a Singleton

One shared PrismaClient instance for the whole app, for exactly the same reason Lesson 1's controllers needed no DI container.

PrismaClient is a class — new PrismaClient() creates an instance that manages its own connection pool to MySQL. Creating more than one of these in a running app is wasteful at best (each opens its own pool) and a real bug at worst, so every part of the app needs to share one instance. Figure 2.13 is the whole of this project's answer to that.

// Figure 2.13: the shared Prisma client (src/config/db.js)
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';

const prisma = new PrismaClient();

export default prisma;

This is the exact same "import = singleton" idea from Lesson 1's controllers-as-plain-functions topic, applied to a real object instead of a group of functions: Node's module loader runs a file's top-level code once, the first time it's imported, and caches the result — every other import prisma from '../config/db.js', anywhere in the app, gets back that same already-constructed instance, not a fresh new PrismaClient() each time. No DI container, no manual setup in app.js to wire a single instance through every layer by hand — just one small file that constructs it, and every service importing that file instead of @prisma/client directly.
